issuer: the Licensing Authority (the Licensing Division of the Ministry of Works and Transport)
note: Read 2026-10-30. The Motor Vehicles and Road Traffic Act, Chap. 48:50, in the Ministry of the Attorney General and Legal Affairs' Digital Legislative Library (laws.gov.tt), the unofficial version updated to 31 December 2016: s. 52, anyone not under 17 and not otherwise disqualified may obtain a driving permit (s. 51 sets 21 for heavy goods and public service vehicles), so the permit is held from 17; s. 58(1)(a), a driving permit expires five years from its issue where the holder is under 61 on that date (renewals for five or ten years under 56, shorter terms from 61); the First Schedule, item (7), as amended by Act 1 of 2016: a five-year permit $500.00, a ten-year permit $1,000.00 (TT dollars). The amending Acts the Library lists from 2017 to No. 2 of 2026 were read for these provisions: none changes s. 52, s. 58 or item (7) (the Finance Act No. 14 of 2025 raises items (13), (22), (23) and (24) of the First Schedule and several penalties; Act 15 of 2020 replaces item (10); Act 2 of 2026 adds fixed penalty warnings). TTConnect's page (the Government's service portal): the permit is managed by the Licensing Division of the Ministry of Works and Transport, and the provisional (learner's) permit is from 17; a provisional permit expires a year from issue (s. 59). No identity card is issued by the Licensing Division and no exchange list was read.
